title: Sandbox client: daemon status reads the daemon's substrate record, not a per-workspace lock nothing writes
goal: SusiDaemonState::check_status (the local fallback behind the mission status report and the leaf /daemon/status) reports a running daemon as running, on any workspace path length
limitations: Windows liveness needs the daemon's byte-range lock on substrate.lock, so the live-case test runs on Linux only; Windows behaviour is daemon_lock_live's, unchanged
other unixes (not release targets) accept the recorded pid, as daemon_lock_live does

results.root_cause: the fallback read <global_dir>/daemon_<hex of workspace path>.lock, which nothing writes since the daemon took one global substrate.lock; the answer was always false (the mission status report always said STOPPED), and for workspace paths over ~120 bytes the file name exceeded the 255-byte limit (seen by T-CLAUDEREL56 as a test failure under a deep TMPDIR)
results.fix: read the pid the daemon records in substrate.pid / substrate.lock and judge it with susi_paths::ports::daemon_lock_live, the same check ports.json readers use; read-only, the workspace path names no file
results.tests: cargo test -p susi-sandbox-client -p susi-leaf-services: all binaries pass (sandbox-client lib 61); new tests check_status_is_false_without_a_live_substrate_record and check_status_sees_the_daemons_substrate_record (the second fails on the old code); fmt; workspace clippy -D warnings; guards architecture 44, core_docs 5, gmcp_requirements 88, lean 2, no_github 5, orphan 3, task_records 3
